fields.name: EEAR[11:8]
fields.text: High bits of the EEPROM address. EEPROM byte address, EEARH and EEARL together, counting linearly from 0 up to E2_END across the 512-byte or 1K-byte EEPROM. Its reset value is undefined, so it must be written before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEAR
fields.text: Low byte of the EEPROM address. EEPROM byte address, EEARH and EEARL together, counting linearly from 0 up to E2_END across the 512-byte or 1K-byte EEPROM. Its reset value is undefined, so it must be written before any EEPROM access.

notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x40.

fields.name: EEDR
fields.text: Byte to be written to EEPROM at the address in EEAR, or, after a read, the byte fetched from that address.

registers.name: EECR
registers.title: The EEPROM Control Register
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x3F.

fields.name: EEPM
fields.text: Picks what a write of EEPE does: erase and write together as one atomic operation, erase only, or write only. Writes to it are ignored while EEPE is 1. Reset returns it to 0b00 unless the EEPROM is in the middle of programming.

rows: Erase and write together, as one atomic operation

fields.name: EERIE
fields.text: 1 enables the EEPROM Ready interrupt when the I bit in SREG is set; 0 disables it. The interrupt keeps firing for as long as EEPE is 0.

fields.name: EEMPE
fields.text: Arms an EEPROM write: while it is 1, setting EEPE within four clock cycles writes the data to the selected address; while it is 0, setting EEPE does nothing. Hardware clears it four clock cycles after software sets it.

fields.name: EEPE
fields.text: Write strobe for the EEPROM: with address and data set up, writing it to 1 starts the write, but only if EEMPE was set to 1 first. Write sequence: wait for EEPE to read 0; wait for SELFPRGEN in SPMCSR to read 0 (needed only when a boot loader can program the Flash); optionally load EEAR and EEDR (in either order); write EEMPE to 1 with EEPE 0; within four clock cycles write EEPE to 1. An interrupt between the last two steps makes the write fail, since EEMPE times out, and an interrupt routine that touches EEAR or EEDR during another EEPROM access spoils that access. No EEPROM write can happen while the CPU is writing the Flash. Hardware clears EEPE when the write time has passed; the CPU stops for two cycles after EEPE is set. Keeping the I bit in SREG clear through every step avoids both failures. Software may poll EEPE for 0 before writing the next byte.

fields.name: EERE
fields.text: Read strobe: with the address in EEAR, writing 1 starts an EEPROM read. The read takes one instruction and the data is ready at once; the CPU stalls four cycles before the next instruction. Poll EEPE first: while a write is under way neither a read nor a change of EEAR is possible. EEPROM accesses are timed by the calibrated oscillator.

registers.title: Oscillator Calibration Register
notes: Initial value of bits 7:0 printed as Device Specific Calibration Value.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x66.

fields.name: CAL
fields.text: Trims the calibrated internal RC oscillator. Reset loads the factory value, which gives 8.0MHz at 25°C; software may write another. The range is ±40%, linear, about 0.4% a step; 0x00 is the lowest frequency and 0xFF the highest, and with typical process at 25°C 8MHz is code 127. Drift with temperature is close to linear but its slope depends on the process; measuring the frequency at two temperatures, which the on-chip temperature sensor makes possible, gives the slope, and the oscillator can then be trimmed against measured temperature. The same oscillator times EEPROM and Flash writes, so those times move with it; above 8.8MHz an EEPROM or Flash write may fail.

fields.name: EXSUT

fields.name: RCE
fields.text: 1 turns the RC oscillator on; 0 turns it off.

fields.name: EXTE

fields.name: CLKS

fields.name: EXCKSEL
fields.text: Clock configuration (CKSEL) for the external clock or low power crystal source, loaded from the fuses at reset when the fuses pick that source. Firmware may change it to set the start-up time after a clock switch. Allowed modes: low power crystal, calibrated internal RC, or external clock only.

fields.name: EXTON

notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x61.

fields.name: CLKPCE
fields.text: Unlocks CLKPS: write it to 1 with every other bit of CLKPR written 0 at the same time, then CLKPS may be changed. Hardware clears it four cycles after the write or when CLKPS is written; writing it again inside those four cycles neither extends nor cancels the window.

fields.name: CLKPS
fields.text: Division factor from the selected clock source to the system clock, writable at run time; all synchronous peripherals slow by the same factor. Reset value comes from the CKDIV8 fuse: 0000 when it is unprogrammed, 0011 (divide by 8) when it is programmed; parts ship with CKDIV8 programmed. Any value can be written whatever CKDIV8 says; software must pick a factor large enough when the clock source is faster than the part's maximum frequency for the operating conditions.

notes: The register summary gives its address as 0x49.

fields.name: PINDIV

fields.name: PLLE
fields.text: 1 starts the PLL. With PINMUX in PLLFRQ also set, setting it turns on the calibrated 8MHz internal RC oscillator as well. The PLL must be off before entering Power-down for the internal RC oscillator to stop and draw no extra current.

fields.name: PLOCK
fields.text: Reads 1 once the PLL has locked to its reference, which takes some ms after enabling. Clearing PLLE clears it.

fields.name: PINMUX

values.text: PLL prescaler, fed by the primary system clock.

fields.name: PLLUSB
fields.text: Division from PLL output to the USB module: 0 passes it straight through (for a 48MHz PLL output); 1 divides it by two (for a 96MHz PLL output).

values.text: No division, for a 48MHz PLL output.
PLL output halved, for a 96MHz PLL output.

fields.name: PLLTM
fields.text: Division factor from the PLL output down to the High Speed Timer clock. Dividing by 1.5 adds clock jitter, though the average duty cycle stays at 50% so the mean error is zero.

fields.name: PDIV
fields.text: Sets the PLL's internal VCO reference for the wanted PLL output frequency. At 5V the best setup is a 96MHz output, divided by 1.5 for a 64MHz High Speed Timer clock and by 2 for a 48MHz USB clock.

notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x60.

fields.name: WDIF
fields.text: Set on a watchdog time-out when the watchdog is set up to interrupt. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1 to it. The time-out interrupt runs when it, WDIE and the I bit in SREG are all set.

fields.name: WDIE
fields.text: With the I bit in SREG set, 1 enables the watchdog interrupt. With WDE 0 the watchdog runs in Interrupt mode and a time-out runs the interrupt. With WDE 1 it runs in Interrupt and System Reset mode: a first time-out sets WDIF, running the vector clears WDIE and WDIF in hardware and the watchdog falls back to System Reset mode, and a further time-out before the interrupt has run resets the system. Keeping that combined mode means setting WDIE again after every interrupt, though not inside the interrupt routine itself.

rows: Interrupt, then switch to System Reset Mode

fields.name: WDP3
fields.text: Watchdog Timer prescaler bit 3. WDP3..0 set the watchdog prescaling, and so the time-out period, while it runs.

fields.name: WDCE
fields.text: Must be 1 to clear WDE or change the prescaler bits, in a timed sequence. Hardware clears it four clock cycles after it is written to 1.

fields.name: WDE
fields.text: Watchdog system reset enable. WDRF in MCUSR overrides it: it stays 1 while WDRF is 1, so WDRF must be cleared before WDE can be. This keeps repeated resets coming while a failure lasts and gives a safe start after it.

fields.name: WDP2

fields.name: WDP1

fields.name: WDP0

fields.name: IVSEL
fields.text: Where the interrupt vectors sit: 0 puts them at the start of Flash, 1 moves them to the start of the boot loader section, whose address the BOOTSZ fuses set. Interrupts are off from the cycle IVCE is set until after the instruction that writes IVSEL, or for four cycles if IVSEL is not written; the I bit in SREG is left alone. fields.name: IVCE

fields.name: TXCIE1
fields.text: 1 enables the Transmit Complete interrupt, raised when TXC1 is set and the SREG global interrupt flag is on.

fields.name: UDRIE1
fields.text: 1 enables the Data Register Empty interrupt, raised when UDRE1 is set and the SREG global interrupt flag is on.

fields.name: RXEN1
fields.text: 1 turns the receiver on and gives it the RxD1 pin. Turning it off flushes the receive buffer and makes FE1, DOR1 and UPE1 invalid.

fields.name: TXEN1
fields.text: 1 turns the transmitter on and gives it the TxD1 pin. Writing 0 takes effect only once the shift register and transmit buffer are empty; the pin then returns to its port function.

fields.name: UCSZ12
fields.text: Third bit of the character size, with UCSZ11:0 in UCSR1C: the number of data bits per frame for receiver and transmitter.

fields.name: RXB81
fields.text: Ninth bit of a received 9-bit character; read it before the low bits in UDR1.

fields.name: TXB81
fields.text: Ninth bit of a 9-bit character to send; write it before the low bits to UDR1.

registers.name: UCSR1C
registers.title: USART Control and Status Register 1 C
notes: Drawn once for every instance, as UCSRnC.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xCA.

fields.name: UMSEL1
fields.text: USART mode.

fields.name: UPM1
fields.text: Parity: off, even or odd. When on, the transmitter adds a parity bit to each frame and the receiver checks it, setting UPE1 on a mismatch.

fields.name: USBS1
fields.text: Number of stop bits the transmitter sends; the receiver ignores it.

fields.name: UCSZ1
fields.text: Low two bits of the character size, with UCSZ12 in UCSR1B: the number of data bits per frame for receiver and transmitter.

fields.name: UCPOL1
fields.text: Synchronous mode only (write 0 in asynchronous mode): which XCK1 edge changes the output data and which samples the input.

columns: Transmitted Data Changed (Output of TxDn Pin)
Received Data Sampled (Input on RxDn Pin)

registers.name: UCSR1D
registers.title: USART Control and Status Register 1 D
notes: Drawn once for every instance, as UCSRnD.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xCB.

fields.name: CTSEN
fields.text: 1 turns on CTS flow control: data is sent only while the CTS input is 0. 0 sends without condition. The pin's DDR bit must be 0 to make it an input.

fields.name: RTSEN
fields.text: 1 turns on RTS flow control: RTS goes high when the receive FIFO is full. 0 turns it off. The pin's DDR bit must be 1 to make it an output.

registers.name: UBRR1H
registers.title: USART Baud Rate Registers
notes: Drawn once for every instance, as UBRRHn.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xCD.

fields.name: UBRR[11:8]
fields.text: Bits 11:8 of the 12-bit USART1 baud rate; UBRR1L holds bits 7:0. Changing the rate corrupts a transfer in progress; a write to UBRR1L updates the baud rate prescaler at once.

registers.name: UBRR1L
registers.title: USART Baud Rate Registers
notes: Drawn once for every instance, as UBRRLn.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xCC.

fields.name: UBRR
fields.text: Bits 7:0 of the 12-bit USART1 baud rate; UBRR1H holds bits 11:8. Changing the rate corrupts a transfer in progress; a write here updates the baud rate prescaler at once.

registers.name: UCSR1A
registers.title: USART MSPIM Control and Status Register 1 A
notes: Drawn once for every instance, as UCSRnA.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xC8.
The register summary prints bit 4 as FE1, bit 3 as DOR1, bit 2 as PE1, bit 1 as U2X1, bit 0 as MPCM1.

fields.name: RXC1
fields.text: 1 while the receive buffer holds unread data, 0 when it is empty; goes to 0 when the receiver is disabled and the buffer flushed. Can raise the Receive Complete interrupt (RXCIE1).

fields.name: TXC1
fields.text: Set when the whole frame has left the transmit shift register and UDR1 holds no new data. Cleared when the Transmit Complete interrupt runs, or by writing 1. Can raise the Transmit Complete interrupt (TXCIE1).

fields.name: UDRE1
fields.text: 1 when the transmit buffer UDR1 is empty and can take new data; set after reset. Can raise the Data Register Empty interrupt (UDRIE).

registers.name: UCSR1B
registers.title: USART MSPIM Control and Status Register 1 B
notes: Drawn once for every instance, as UCSRnB.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xC9.

fields.name: RXCIE1
fields.text: 1 enables the Receive Complete interrupt, raised when RXC1 is set and the SREG global interrupt flag is on.

fields.name: TXCIE1
fields.text: 1 enables the Transmit Complete interrupt, raised when TXC1 is set and the SREG global interrupt flag is on.

fields.name: UDRIE
fields.text: 1 enables the Data Register Empty interrupt, raised when UDRE1 is set and the SREG global interrupt flag is on.

fields.name: RXEN1
fields.text: 1 turns the receiver on in MSPIM mode and gives it the RxD1 pin; turning it off flushes the receive buffer. The receiver alone (RXEN1 = 1, TXEN1 = 0) does nothing, as the transmitter drives the clock and only master mode exists.

fields.name: TXEN1
fields.text: 1 turns the transmitter on and gives it the TxD1 pin. Writing 0 takes effect only once the shift register and transmit buffer are empty; the pin then returns to its port function.

registers.name: UCSR1C
registers.title: USART MSPIM Control and Status Register 1 C
notes: Drawn once for every instance, as UCSRnC.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xCA.

fields.name: UMSEL1
fields.text: USART mode; both bits 1 select MSPIM. UDORD1, UCPHA1 and UCPOL1 may be written in the same write that turns MSPIM on.

fields.name: UDORD1
fields.text: Bit order: 1 sends the LSB first, 0 the MSB first.

fields.name: UCPHA1
fields.text: Picks the XCK1 edge that samples data: the first (leading) one or the last (trailing) one.

fields.name: UCPOL1
fields.text: Polarity of the XCK1 clock; with UCPHA1 it sets the transfer timing.

registers.name: TWBR
registers.title: TWI Bit Rate Register
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xB8.

fields.name: TWBR
fields.text: Division factor of the bit rate generator, which makes the SCL frequency in master modes.

registers.name: TWCR
registers.title: TWI Control Register
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xBC.

fields.name: TWINT
fields.text: Set by hardware when the TWI finishes a job and waits for software; SCL low is stretched while it is set. With TWIE and the SREG I-bit set the TWI interrupt runs. Not cleared by the interrupt; software clears it by writing 1, which starts the next TWI operation, so TWAR, TWSR and TWDR accesses must be done first.

fields.name: TWEA
fields.text: 1 makes the TWI send ACK when its own slave address arrives, when a general call arrives with TWGCE set, or when a data byte arrives in master or slave receiver mode. 0 takes the device off the bus for a time; writing 1 again resumes address recognition.

fields.name: TWSTA
fields.text: Write 1 to become bus master: the TWI sends a START when the bus is free, or waits for a STOP and then sends one. Software must clear it once the START has gone out.

fields.name: TWSTO
fields.text: In master mode, 1 sends a STOP; the bit clears itself when the STOP is done. In slave mode, 1 recovers from an error with no STOP sent: the TWI returns to unaddressed slave mode and releases SCL and SDA to high impedance.

fields.name: TWWC
fields.text: Set by a write to TWDR while TWINT is low; cleared by a write to TWDR while TWINT is high.

fields.name: TWEN
fields.text: 1 turns the TWI on: it takes the SCL and SDA pins, with slew-rate limiters and spike filters. 0 turns it off and ends any transfer at once.

fields.name: TWIE
fields.text: 1, with the SREG I-bit set, requests the TWI interrupt for as long as TWINT is high.

registers.name: TWSR
registers.title: TWI Status Register
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xB9.

fields.name: TWS
fields.text: 5-bit status of the TWI logic and bus. A read of TWSR also holds the 2 prescaler bits, which should be masked off when reading the status.

fields.name: TWPS
fields.text: Bit rate prescaler, readable and writable; used in the bit rate formula.

registers.name: TWDR
registers.title: TWI Data Register
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xBB.

fields.name: TWD
fields.text: Next byte to send, or last byte received, on the bus.

registers.name: TWAR
registers.title: TWI (Slave) Address Register
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xBA.

fields.name: TWA
fields.text: 7-bit slave address of the TWI.

fields.name: TWGCE
fields.text: 1 turns on recognition of a General Call on the bus.

registers.name: TWAMR
registers.title: TWI (Slave) Address Mask Register
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xBD.

fields.name: TWAM
fields.text: 7-bit mask on the slave address: a bit set to 1 makes the address match ignore the matching TWAR bit of the incoming address.

registers.name: UHWCON
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xD7.

fields.name: UVREGE
fields.text: 1 turns the USB pad regulator on, 0 off.

registers.name: USBCON
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xD8.

fields.name: USBE
fields.text: 1 turns the USB controller on. 0 turns it off and resets it, and turns off the USB transceiver and the controller's clock inputs.

fields.name: FRZCLK
fields.text: 1 stops the USB clock inputs, lowering power; resume detection stays on. 0 runs them.

fields.name: OTGPADE
fields.text: 1 turns the VBUS pad on, 0 off. Works with USBE = 0, so VBUS can be detected with the USB macro off.

fields.name: VBUSTE
fields.text: 1 enables the VBUS transition interrupt, 0 disables it.

registers.name: USBSTA
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xD9.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Always reads 1; kept for compatibility with AT90USB64/128, where it gives the OTG ID pin.

fields.name: VBUS
fields.text: Reads the state of the VBUS pin; in device mode it shows whether the USB bus is connected.

registers.name: USBINT
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xDA.

fields.name: VBUSTI
fields.text: Set by hardware on a VBUS pad transition, high to low or low to high. Cleared by software.

registers.name: UDCON
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xE0.

fields.name: RSTCPU
fields.text: 1 resets the CPU when a USB End of Reset is detected, while the USB controller stays enabled and attached. Cleared when the USB controller is disabled; the CPU reset it causes leaves it set.

fields.name: LSM
fields.text: In device mode, selects the speed: 0 full speed (D+ pull-up on when ATTACH is set), 1 low speed (D- pull-up on when ATTACH is set). No effect in host mode.

fields.name: RMWKUP
fields.text: 1 sends an upstream resume to the host for remote wake-up, only while SUSPI is set. Hardware clears it once the signalling ends; software clearing does nothing.

fields.name: DETACH
fields.text: 1 detaches the device by disconnecting the internal D+ or D- pull-up; 0 reconnects it.

registers.name: UDINT
notes: The Read/Write row is blank.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xE1.
The register summary prints bit 1 as MSOFI.

fields.name: UPRSMI
fields.text: Set by hardware while the USB controller sends an upstream resume; raises a USB interrupt if UPRSME is set. Cleared by software, with the USB clocks running; software setting does nothing.

fields.name: EORSMI
fields.text: Set by hardware when a valid End Of Resume from the host is detected; raises a USB interrupt if EORSME is set. Cleared by software; software setting does nothing.

fields.name: WAKEUPI
fields.text: Hardware sets it when a filtered non-idle signal on the lines re-activates the USB controller (an upstream resume does not); raises an interrupt if WAKEUPE is set. Cleared by software, with the USB clock inputs running; software setting does nothing.

fields.name: EORSTI
fields.text: Hardware sets it on detecting an End Of Reset; raises a USB interrupt if EORSTE is set. Cleared by software; software setting does nothing.

fields.name: SOFI
fields.text: Set by hardware when a USB Start Of Frame PID is detected, every 1 ms; raises a USB interrupt if SOFE is set.

fields.name: SUSPI
fields.text: Suspend interrupt flag. Cleared by software; software setting does nothing. Like all these flags, it is set whether or not its enable bit is.

registers.name: UDIEN
notes: The Read/Write row is blank.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xE2.
The register summary prints bit 1 as MSOFE.

fields.name: UPRSME
fields.text: 1 enables the UPRSMI interrupt, 0 disables it.

fields.name: EORSME
fields.text: 1 enables the EORSMI interrupt, 0 disables it.

fields.name: WAKEUPE
fields.text: 1 enables the WAKEUPI interrupt, 0 disables it.

fields.name: EORSTE
fields.text: 1 enables the EORSTI interrupt, 0 disables it; set after reset.

fields.name: SOFE
fields.text: 1 enables the SOFI interrupt, 0 disables it.

fields.name: SUSPE
fields.text: 1 enables the SUSPI interrupt, 0 disables it.

registers.name: UDADDR
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xE3.

fields.name: ADDEN
fields.text: 1 makes the address in UADD active. Cleared by hardware; software clearing does nothing.

fields.name: UADD
fields.text: Device USB address, written by software.

registers.name: UDFNUMH
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xE5.

fields.name: FNUM[10:8]
fields.text: High 3 bits of the 11-bit frame number, written by hardware from the last SOF packet received; updated even when that SOF is corrupted.

registers.name: UDFNUML
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xE4.

fields.name: FNUM
fields.text: Low 8 bits of the 11-bit frame number, written by hardware.

registers.name: UDMFN
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xE6.

fields.name: FNCERR
fields.text: Set by hardware when a start of frame packet arrives with a corrupted frame number; updated together with SOFI.

registers.name: UENUM
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xE9.

fields.name: EPNUM
fields.text: Number of the endpoint the CPU accesses, written by software. 111b is not allowed.

registers.name: UERST
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xEA.

fields.name: EPRST
fields.text: One bit per endpoint: 1 resets that endpoint's FIFO, before any other operation, after a hardware reset or after a USB bus reset. Software then writes 0 to finish the reset and use the endpoint.

registers.name: UECONX
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xEB.

fields.name: STALLRQ
fields.text: 1 answers the host's next handshake with STALL. Cleared by hardware when a new SETUP arrives; software clearing does nothing.

fields.name: STALLRQC
fields.text: 1 turns off the STALL handshake. Cleared by hardware right after it is set; software clearing does nothing.

fields.name: RSTDT
fields.text: 1 resets the data toggle: the next OUT packet received, or the next IN packet sent, uses toggle 0. Cleared by hardware at once, so firmware need not wait; software clearing does nothing.

fields.name: EPEN
fields.text: 1 enables the endpoint per the device configuration; 0 disables it. Endpoint 0 must be enabled after any hardware or USB reset.

registers.name: UECFG0X
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xEC.

fields.name: EPTYPE
fields.text: Endpoint type: 00b Control, 01b Isochronous, 10b Bulk, 11b Interrupt.

fields.name: EPDIR
fields.text: 1 makes a bulk, interrupt or isochronous endpoint IN; 0 makes a bulk, interrupt, isochronous or control endpoint OUT.

registers.name: UECFG1X
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xED.

fields.name: EPSIZE
fields.text: Endpoint size: 000b 8 bytes, 001b 16, 010b 32, 011b 64, 100b 128, 101b 256, 110b 512 bytes; 111b reserved, not to be used.

fields.name: EPBK
fields.text: Number of banks: 00b one, 01b two; 1xb reserved, not to be used.

fields.name: ALLOC
fields.text: 1 allocates the endpoint's memory, 0 frees it.

registers.name: UESTA0X
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xEE.

fields.name: CFGOK
fields.text: Set by hardware when EPSIZE and EPBK fit the largest FIFO size and bank count; updated when ALLOC is set. If 0, UECFG1X should be written again with valid EPSIZE and EPBK.

fields.name: OVERFI
fields.text: Set by hardware on an overflow in an isochronous endpoint; triggers EPINTx if enabled. Cleared by software; software setting does nothing.

fields.name: UNDERFI
fields.text: Set by hardware on an underflow in an isochronous endpoint; triggers EPINTx if enabled. Cleared by software; software setting does nothing.

fields.name: DTSEQ
fields.text: Set by hardware to the data PID of the current bank: 00b Data0, 01b Data1, 1xb reserved. For OUT, the toggle last received in that bank; for IN, the toggle the next packet will use, independent of the current bank.

fields.name: NBUSYBK
fields.text: Set by hardware to the number of busy banks: for IN, banks filled by the user and ready to send; for OUT, banks filled by the host. 00b all free, 01b one busy, 10b two busy, 11b reserved.

registers.name: UESTA1X
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xEF.

fields.name: CTRLDIR
fields.text: Set by hardware after a SETUP packet to the direction of the next packet: 1 IN, 0 OUT. Software cannot change it.

fields.name: CURRBK
fields.text: Set by hardware to the current bank of any endpoint other than control: 00b Bank0, 01b Bank1, 1xb reserved. Software cannot change it.

registers.name: UEINTX
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xE8.

fields.name: FIFOCON
fields.text: OUT and SETUP endpoints: set by hardware, with RXOUTI or RXSTPI, when a new OUT message lands in the current bank; clearing it frees the bank and moves to the next. IN endpoints: set by hardware, with TXINI, when the current bank is free; clearing it sends the FIFO data and moves to the next bank. Software setting does nothing.

fields.name: NAKINI
fields.text: Set by hardware when a NAK has been sent for an IN request from the host; raises a USB interrupt if NAKINE is set. Cleared by software; software setting does nothing.

fields.name: RWAL
fields.text: Set by hardware when, for IN, the current bank is not full and firmware can write the FIFO, or, for OUT, it is not empty and firmware can read it. Never set while STALLRQ is set or on an error; cleared by hardware otherwise. Not for the control endpoint.

fields.name: NAKOUTI
fields.text: Set by hardware when a NAK has been sent for an OUT or PING request from the host; raises a USB interrupt if NAKOUTE is set. Cleared by software; software setting does nothing.

fields.name: RXSTPI
fields.text: Set by hardware when the current bank holds a new valid SETUP packet; triggers EPINTx if enabled. Software clears it to acknowledge; software setting does nothing. Stays 0 on an IN endpoint.

fields.name: RXOUTI
fields.text: RXOUTI: set by hardware when the current bank holds a new packet; triggers EPINTx if enabled; software clears it to acknowledge, and setting it does nothing. KILLBK (IN endpoints): 1 discards the last written bank; cleared by hardware once done; software clearing does nothing.

fields.name: STALLEDI
fields.text: Set by hardware when a STALL has been sent, or a CRC error is found on an OUT isochronous endpoint. Cleared by software; software setting does nothing.

fields.name: TXINI
fields.text: Hardware sets it when the current bank is empty and can be filled; triggers EPINTx if enabled. Software clears it to acknowledge; software setting does nothing. Stays 0 on an OUT endpoint.

registers.name: UEIENX
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xF0.

fields.name: FLERRE
fields.text: 1 raises the endpoint interrupt (EPINTx) on OVERFI or UNDERFI; 0 does not.

fields.name: NAKINE
fields.text: 1 raises the endpoint interrupt (EPINTx) when NAKINI is set; 0 does not.

fields.name: NAKOUTE
fields.text: 1 raises the endpoint interrupt (EPINTx) when NAKOUTI is set; 0 does not.

fields.name: RXSTPE
fields.text: 1 raises the endpoint interrupt (EPINTx) on RXSTPI; 0 does not.

fields.name: RXOUTE
fields.text: 1 raises the endpoint interrupt (EPINTx) on RXOUTI; 0 does not.

fields.name: STALLEDE
fields.text: 1 raises the endpoint interrupt (EPINTx) on STALLEDI; 0 does not.

fields.name: TXINE
fields.text: 1 raises the endpoint interrupt (EPINTx) on TXINI; 0 does not.

registers.name: UEDATX
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xF1.

fields.name: DATD
fields.text: Byte read from or written to the endpoint FIFO chosen by EPNUM.

registers.name: UEBCHX
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xF3.

fields.name: BYCTD[10:8]
fields.text: High 3 bits of the endpoint FIFO byte count, written by hardware; UEBCLX holds the low byte.

registers.name: UEBCLX
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xF2.

fields.name: BYCTD
fields.text: Low byte of the 11-bit endpoint FIFO byte count, written by hardware. For IN it goes up with each byte written and down with each byte sent; for OUT it goes up with each byte from the host and down with each byte software reads.

registers.name: UEINT
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0xF4.

fields.name: EPINTD
fields.text: One bit per endpoint, set by hardware when that endpoint's UEINTX raises an interrupt with its enable bit set; cleared by hardware when the source is served.

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x7B.

fields.name: ADHSM
fields.text: ADC High Speed Mode.

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: 1, with the ADC off (ADEN = 0), connects the ADC multiplexer to the comparator's negative input; 0 connects the bandgap reference there.

fields.name: MUX5
fields.text: Analog channel selection bit 5.

fields.name: ADTS3
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source bit 3.

fields.name: ADTS2
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source bit 2.

fields.name: ADTS1
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source bit 1.

fields.name: ADTS0
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source bit 0.

registers.name: ACSR
registers.title: Analog Comparator Control and Status Register
notes: Initial value of bit 5 printed as N/A.
The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x50.

fields.name: ACD
fields.text: 1 cuts power to the Analog Comparator, lowering power in Active and Idle; may be set at any time. Clear ACIE before changing it, or an interrupt may occur.

fields.name: ACBG
fields.text: 1 puts a fixed bandgap reference on the comparator's positive input; 0 puts AIN0 there.

fields.name: ACO
fields.text: Comparator output, synchronized, so 1 to 2 clock cycles late.

fields.name: ACI
fields.text: Hardware sets it when the comparator output makes the event chosen by ACIS1:0. With ACIE and the SREG I-bit set the interrupt runs. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: ACIE
fields.text: 1, with the SREG I-bit set, enables the Analog Comparator interrupt; 0 disables it.

fields.name: ACIC
fields.text: 1 lets the comparator trigger the Timer/Counter1 input capture; its output then feeds the capture front end and uses its noise canceler and edge select. 0 leaves them unconnected. ICIE1 in TIMSK1 must be set for the capture interrupt.

fields.name: ACIS
fields.text: Comparator event that triggers the interrupt. Clear ACIE before changing these bits, or an interrupt may occur.

registers.name: DIDR1
registers.title: Digital Input Disable Register 1
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x7F.

fields.name: AIN0D
fields.text: 1 turns off the AIN0 digital input buffer; its PIN bit then reads 0. Meant for an analog signal whose digital value is not needed, to save power in the buffer.

registers.name: ADMUX
registers.title: ADC Multiplexer Selection Register
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x7C.

fields.name: REFS
fields.text: ADC voltage reference. A change during a conversion takes effect when it ends (ADIF set). The internal references cannot be used with an external voltage on AREF.

values.text: Internal 2.56 V, external capacitor on AREF.

fields.name: ADLAR
fields.text: 1 left-adjusts the result in the ADC data register, 0 right-adjusts it; takes effect at once, even during a conversion.

fields.name: MUX
fields.text: With MUX5 in ADCSRB, picks the analog inputs connected to the ADC and the gain of the differential channels. A change during a conversion takes effect when it ends (ADIF set).

registers.name: ADCSRA
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register A
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x7A.

fields.name: ADEN
fields.text: 1 turns the ADC on; 0 turns it off and stops any conversion in progress.

fields.name: ADSC
fields.text: Write 1 to start a conversion (Single Conversion), or the first one (Free Running). The first conversion after enabling takes 25 ADC clocks instead of 13 and initializes the ADC. Reads 1 while converting, 0 when done; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ADATE
fields.text: 1 turns on auto triggering: a conversion starts on a rising edge of the trigger chosen by ADTS in ADCSRB.

fields.name: ADIF
fields.text: Set at the end of a conversion, once ADCH/ADCL hold the new result; with ADIE and the SREG I-bit set the interrupt runs. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. A read-modify-write of ADCSRA, including SBI and CBI, can clear a pending interrupt.

fields.name: ADIE
fields.text: 1, with the SREG I-bit set, enables the ADC Conversion Complete interrupt.

fields.name: ADPS
fields.text: Division factor from the XTAL clock to the ADC clock.

registers.name: ADCH
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x79.

notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x78.

fields.name: ADC7

fields.name: ADC6

fields.text: ADC result bit 5 (right-adjusted).

fields.name: ADTS
fields.text: Trigger source for a conversion when ADATE is 1; no effect when ADATE is 0. The rising edge of the chosen flag starts a conversion, so switching from a clear source to a set one makes an edge and, with ADEN set, starts one. Switching to Free Running (0) makes no trigger even with ADIF set.

registers.title: MCU Control Register
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x55.

fields.name: JTD
fields.text: 0 leaves JTAG on when the JTAGEN fuse is programmed; 1 turns JTAG off. A change takes the same value written twice within four cycles. Not to be changed while the on-chip debug system is in use.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: 1 turns off the pull-ups of all I/O ports, even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn ask for one ({DDxn, PORTxn} = 0b01).

fields.name: IVSEL
fields.text: 0 puts the interrupt vectors at the start of Flash; 1 moves them to the start of the boot loader section, whose address the BOOTSZ fuses set. To change it, write IVCE to 1, then within four cycles write IVSEL with IVCE at 0. Interrupts are off from the cycle IVCE is set until after the instruction that writes IVSEL, or four cycles if IVSEL is not written; the I-bit in SREG is left alone. With vectors in the boot loader section and BLB02 programmed, interrupts are off while running from the application section; with vectors in the application section and BLB12 programmed, they are off while running from the boot loader section.

fields.name: IVCE
fields.text: Written 1 to allow a change of IVSEL, and turns interrupts off. Hardware clears it four cycles after the write, or when IVSEL is written.

fields.name: JTRF
fields.text: Set when a reset comes from a 1 in the JTAG Reset Register, chosen by the AVR_RESET JTAG instruction. Writing 0 clears it, as does a power-on reset.

fields.name: WDRF

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register
notes: The diagram prints no address; the register summary gives 0x57.

fields.name: SPMIE
fields.text: Written 1 with the Status Register I-bit set, enables the SPM ready interrupt, which runs for as long as SPMCSR.SPMEN is 0.

fields.name: RWWSB
fields.text: Set by hardware when self-programming (erasing or writing a page) of the RWW section starts; while set, the RWW section is inaccessible. Cleared by writing RWWSRE to 1 once the self-programming finishes, or on its own when a page load starts.

fields.name: SIGRD
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes an LPM within the next three clock cycles load a signature-row byte into its destination register; an SPM within four cycles of setting SIGRD and SPMEN does nothing. Reserved for future use; not to be used.

fields.name: RWWSRE
fields.text: Once erasing or writing a page in the RWW section has finished (SPMEN back at 0), writing RWWSRE to 1 together with SPMEN makes an SPM within four clock cycles reopen the RWW section for reading. It cannot be reopened while SPMEN is set; writing RWWSRE during a Flash load aborts the load and loses the loaded data.

fields.name: BLBSET
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes an SPM within the next four clock cycles set the Boot Lock bits from R0, ignoring R1 and the Z-pointer. Clears itself when the lock bits are set or when four cycles pass with no SPM. An (E)LPM within three cycles of setting BLBSET and SPMEN loads the Lock bits or the Fuse bits, chosen by Z0 of the Z-pointer, into its destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes an SPM in the following four clock cycles program the temporary buffer into the page given by the upper Z-pointer bits, ignoring R1 and R0. Clears itself when the write finishes or when four cycles pass with no SPM. The CPU halts for the whole write if the NRWW section is the target.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Written 1 together with SPMEN, makes an SPM within the next four clock cycles erase the page given by the upper Z-pointer bits, ignoring R1 and R0. Clears itself when the erase finishes or when four cycles pass with no SPM. The CPU halts for the whole operation if the NRWW section is the target.

fields.name: SPMEN
fields.text: Allows the SPM instruction for the following four clock cycles. Written with RWWSRE, BLBSET, PGWRT or PGERS, the next SPM does that bit's operation; written alone, the next SPM puts R1:R0 into the temporary page buffer at the Z-pointer address, Z-pointer LSB ignored. Clears itself after the SPM or when four cycles pass with none, but stays 1 until a Page Erase or Page Write completes. Only 10001, 01001, 00101, 00011 and 00001 in the low five bits have an effect; one SPM at a time.
